He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's Hawks]]. Hall has played in nine [[NBA]] games for the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. ==High school career== Raised in [[North Wildwood, New Jersey]], Hall played basketball for [[Middle Township High School]] in [[Cape May Court House, New Jersey]] as a freshman before transferring to [[Cardinal O'Hara High School (Springfield, Pennsylvania)|Cardinal O'Hara High School]] in [[Springfield Township, Delaware County, Pennsylvania|Springfield, Pennsylvania]].{{cite web |last1=Zimmaro |first1=Mark |title=Jordan Hall fitting in with high-flying Neumann-Goretti |url=https://southphillyreview.com/2020/01/13/jordan-hall-fitting-in-with-high-flying-neumann-goretti/ |website=South Philly Review |access-date=June 13, 2021 |date=January 13, 2020}}[https://coastsportstoday.com/2019/06/cape-may-county-native-commits-to-play-division-i-basketball/ "Cape May County native commits to play Division I basketball"], ''Coast Sports Today'', June 25, 2019. Accessed May 11, 2022. "Jordan Hall, a rising senior and 6-7 guard/forward at Neumann-Goretti High School in the Philadelphia Catholic League, has verbally committed to play at St. Joseph’s University, according to various media reports. Hall attended Margaret Mace Elementary School in North Wildwood and spent his freshman season at Middle Township High School." Entering his junior year, he moved to [[Saints John Neumann and Maria Goretti Catholic High School]] in [[Philadelphia|Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]].{{cite web |last1=Callahan |first1=Kevin |title=St. Joe's-bound Jordan Hall has grown into versatile star for Neumann-Goretti |url=https://www.cityofbasketballlove.com/news_article/show/1081160 |website=City of Basketball Love |access-date=June 13, 2021 |date=January 27, 2020}} As a senior, Hall led his team to a [[Philadelphia Catholic League]] title and was named Catholic League Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Gifford |first1=Matt |title=Hall ready for Hawk Hill |url=https://247sports.com/college/saint-josephs/Article/Deep-dive-into-the-game-of-incoming-Hawk-Jordan-Hall-147050060/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=June 13, 2021 |date=May 11, 2020}} He was a First Team Class 3A All-State selection.{{cite web |last1=Anastasia |first1=Phil |title=First-team choice Jordan Hall among four Neumann Goretti basketball players named to Class 3A all-state squads |url=https://www.inquirer.com/high-school-sports/pennsylvania/piaa-basketball-class-3a-first-team-all-state-20200429.html |website=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |access-date=June 13, 2021 |date=April 29, 2020}} Hall committed to playing college basketball for [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's]] over offers from [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle]] and [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green]].{{cite web |last1=Narducci |first1=Mark |title=Neumann-Goretti's Jordan Hall commits to St. Joe's; is Billy Lange's first class of 2020 recruit |url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/st-joes/st-joes-recruiting-billy-lange-neumann-goretti-jordan-hall-20190625.html |website=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |access-date=June 13, 2021 |date=June 25, 2019}} ==College career== On February 20, 2021, Hall recorded a freshman season-high 22 points, 12 rebounds and 10 assists in a 91–82 overtime win over La Salle, the fourth [[triple-double]] in Saint Joseph's history.{{cite web |title=Daly Drops 30, Hall Records Triple-Double in Men's Basketball's 91-82 OT Win over La Salle |url=https://sjuhawks.com/news/2021/2/20/daly-drops-30-hall-triple-double-in-mens-basketballs-91-82-ot-win-over-la-salle.aspx |website=Saint Joseph's University |access-date=June 12, 2021 |date=February 20, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 10.6 points, 5.9 rebounds and 5.7 assists per game, earning [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] All-Rookie Team honors.{{cite web |last1=Cole |first1=Damichael |title=Atlantic-10 all-rookie selection Jordan Hall entering transfer portal, leaving St. Joe's |url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/st-joes/jordan-hall-transfer-portal-st-joes-20210428.html |website=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |access-date=June 12, 2021 |date=April 28, 2021}} Hall led all [[NCAA Division I]] freshmen in assists.{{cite web |last1=Cole |first1=Damichael |title=Former St. Joseph's forward Jordan Hall headed to Texas A&M |url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/st-joes/jordan-hall-transfers-texas-am-20210504.html |website=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |access-date=June 12, 2021 |date=May 4, 2021}} After the season, he left the program for personal reasons.{{cite web |last1=Holmes |first1=C.J. |title=Why Saint Joseph's star freshman Jordan Hall entered the transfer portal, and what it means for the Hawks |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2552125/2021/04/29/why-saint-josephs-star-freshman-jordan-hall-entered-the-transfer-portal-and-what-it-means-for-the-hawks/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=June 12, 2021 |date=April 29, 2021}} Hall initially decided to transfer to [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]] and declare for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Underwood |first1=Hannah |title=Texas A&M men's basketball inks St. Joseph's transfer Jordan Hall |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/texas-am-aggies/2021/05/04/texas-am-mens-basketball-inks-st-josephs-transfer-jordan-hall/ |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=June 12, 2021 |date=May 4, 2021}}{{Cite tweet |ref= |last=Zagoria |first=Adam |user=AdamZagoria |number=1397380410284335104 |date=May 25, 2021 |title=Texas A&M transfer commit Jordan Hall will test the NBA Draft waters, per source. |access-date=June 13, 2021}} However, on June 30 he announced he was withdrawing from the draft and returning to Saint Joseph's instead of transferring to Texas A&M.{{cite news |last1=Hattersley |first1=Andrew |title=Report: Jordan Hall withdraws name from NBA Draft, returning to St. Joe's |url=https://247sports.com/college/texas-am/Article/Jordan-Hall-Withdraws-name-NBA-Draft-Returning-St-Josephs-Texas-AM-Basketball-Buzz-Williams--167234389/ |access-date=July 4, 2021 |work=247 Sports |date=June 30, 2021}} As a sophomore, Hall led Saint Joseph's in scoring with 14.1 points per game while also averaging 6.7 rebounds, 5.8 assists, and 1.2 steals per game. On March 18, 2022, he declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Klingman |first1=Nicholas |title=St. Joseph’s guard Jordan Hall will decline remaining eligibility, declare for the NBA draft |url=https://www.inquirer.com/sports/st-josephs-university-st-joes-ncaa-nba-draft-mens-basketball-jordan-hall-20220318.html |access-date=March 21, 2022 |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=March 18, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===San Antonio Spurs (2022)=== After going undrafted in [[2022 NBA draft]], on August 11, 2022, Hall signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite news |title=SPURS SIGN JORDAN HALL TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-jordan-hall-to-two-way-contract |access-date=August 14, 2022 |website=NBA.com |date=August 11, 2022}} He was initially waived on October 24, without having played in a game,{{Cite web |title=SPURS SIGN CHARLES BASSEY TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT |url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-charles-bassey-to-two-way-contract |access-date=2022-10-27 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}} but later on November 2, the Spurs re-signed Hall.{{cite web|title=Spurs sign Jordan Hall|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-jordan-hall|date=November 2, 2022|website=NBA.com|accessdate=November 2, 2022}} Hall made his [[NBA]] debut on the same day, coming off the bench and scoring three points, two assists and a rebound in a 100–143 loss to [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|title=Siakam, Trent help Raptors overwhelm depleted Spurs, 143-100|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468269|date=November 2, 2022|website=ESPN.com|accessdate=November 3, 2022}} On November 29, 2022, Hall was waived by the Spurs.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-sign-alize-johnson-2|website=nba.com|title=SPURS SIGN ALIZE JOHNSON|access-date=November 29, 2022|date=November 29, 2022}} ===Austin Spurs (2022–2023)=== On December 1, 2022, Hall signed with the [[Austin Spurs]].{{cite tweet|author=Austin Spurs|title=Help us welcome Jordan Hall to ATX! He will be available in tonight’s game. 👏|number=1598492305463336961|user=austin_spurs|date=December 1, 2022|access-date=December 1, 2022}} ===Long Island Nets (2023–2024)=== On August 31, 2023, Hall's rights were traded to the [[Long Island Nets]]{{cite web|title=Long Island Nets Acquire Returning Player Rights to Jordan Hall|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/long-island-nets-acquire-returning-player-rights-to-jordan-hall/n-6008697|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=August 31, 2023|access-date=August 31, 2023}} and on September 20, he signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite tweet|first=Keith|last=Smith|title=The Brooklyn Nets announced they have signed guard/forward Jordan Hall and guard Keifer Sykes.|number=1704544324162085185|user=KeithSmithNBA|date=September 20, 2023|access-date=September 26, 2023}} However, they waived him on September 25.{{cite tweet|first=Keith|last=Smith|title=The Brooklyn Nets announced they have waived Jordan Hall and Keifer Sykes. The Nets have signed Kyler Edwards.|number=1706366757449990303|user=KeithSmithNBA|date=September 25, 2023|access-date=September 26, 2023}} On October 28, he joined Long Island.{{cite web|title=Patrick Gardner, Kennedy Chandler, two-ways top Long Island Nets training camp roster|url=https://www.netsdaily.com/2023/10/28/23936762/patrick-gardner-kennedy-chandler-two-ways-top-long-island-nets-training-camp-roster|website=NetsDaily.com|date=October 28, 2023|access-date=November 12, 2023}} ===GeVi Napoli (2024)=== On August 1, 2024, Hall signed with [[Napoli Basket (2016)|GeVi Napoli]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]],{{cite web|title=NAPOLI BASKET, INGAGGIATO JORDAN HALL|url=https://napolibasket.it/napoli-basket-ingaggiato-jordan-hall/|website=NapoliBasket.it.com|date=August 1, 2024|access-date=August 1, 2024|language=Italian}} but he got waived by the team on October 15 after just 3 games with the team.{{cite web|title=UFFICIALE - Napoli Basket, Jordan Hall fuori squadra per motivi di natura tecnica|url=https://www.calcionapoli24.it/basket/ufficiale-napoli-basket-jordan-hall-escluso-dallattivit-della-prima-squadra-per-n621887.html|website=CalcioNapoli24.it|date=October 15, 2024|access-date=October 17, 2024|language=it}} ===Windy City Bulls (2024)=== On November 7, 2024, Hall signed with the [[Windy City Bulls]].{{cite web|title=Windy City Bulls Announce 2024-25 Opening Night Roster|url=https://windycity.gleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-bulls-announce-2024-25-opening-night-roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 7, 2024|access-date=November 12, 2024}} ===Texas Legends (2025–2026)=== On March 14, 2025, Hall signed with the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite web |title=LEGENDS SIGN GUARD JORDAN HALL |url=https://texas.gleague.nba.com/news/legends-sign-guard-jordan-hall |website=Texas Legends |access-date=8 July 2025 |language=en}} ===Santa Cruz Warriors (2026–present)=== On March 20, 2026, [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] announced that they had signed Hall.{{cite
